_comment: 🧩️ This subset's own contribution. `s.trinity.rewrite` is a semio-NATIVE graph-rewrite RULE document — three whole JSON documents carried as strings plus two string-keyed maps — not a rewriting engine, so a rewriting library has nothing to adjudicate. The reference is a SECOND IMPLEMENTATION in Python written from this subset's committed snapshot schema, mutation grammar and specification vectors.

oracles.rationale: A second implementation of the `s.trinity.rewrite` rule document and all seven typed mutations, in Python, at `../../../../../🧪️tests/mutate-rewrite-1/🐍️component.py`. Written from `../🧬️schema/📸️snapshot/🔣️component.json` (the five members, with the three `contentMediaType: application/json` strings and the two maps), `../🧬️schema/🧬️mutations/📝️text/📖️component.grammar.semio` (the seven verbs and their positional argument lists) and the seven committed `(before, mutation, after, outcome)` specification vectors. It imports nothing from this repository and transliterates none of its Rust. A third-party library was declined, not merely absent: GrGen, AGG and `networkx`'s isomorphism module implement graph REWRITING, while this artifact is the rule DOCUMENT — a before-fixture, a pattern, a right-hand side, the parameter bindings and the editor layout — which none of them models, none reads `.dsl.semio`, and none has an opinion on whether `change-parameter-binding` on an absent key inserts or refuses. This reference deliberately does NOT read the carrier: `.rewrite.dsl.semio` has no prose document and mixes three value encodings in one file — a backslash-escaped quoted string, a braced block and a fenced ```json block — with nothing stating which member gets which, so the reading is done once in a recorded derivation script and the carrier's own byte-exact law stays asserted in role on the Rust side. `package` is deliberately empty: the implementation needs no distribution, so this entry contributes nothing to `🔒️dependencies.json`.
